security_audit.summary: All 80 static findings are false positives caused by KEGG REST calls, documentation formatting, biological identifiers, or ordinary example text. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, shell execution, reconnaissance, or path traversal evidence was found.

remediation.issue: Network requests have no explicit timeout.
remediation.suggestion: Set a finite timeout for each request and handle URL and timeout errors.

remediation.issue: URL path parameters are interpolated without dedicated validation.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist database and option values, then encode each path component before requesting KEGG.

remediation.issue: Image responses are decoded as UTF-8 text.
remediation.suggestion: Return bytes for image requests and decode only documented text formats.

content.user_title: Explore KEGG Pathways and Molecular Data
content.value_statement: Finding connected biological records across KEGG can require several REST operations and careful identifier handling. This skill supplies focused helpers and references for reproducible academic queries.
actual_capabilities: Query KEGG database metadata and list database or organism entries.
Search genes, compounds, and drugs by keywords, formulas, or molecular ranges.
Retrieve up to ten KEGG entries, including sequences, structures, KGML, and pathway JSON.
Convert KEGG identifiers to supported NCBI, UniProt, PubChem, and ChEBI identifiers.
Link genes, pathways, compounds, reactions, enzymes, and orthology records.
Retrieve KEGG drug interaction records for up to ten drug identifiers.
limitations: KEGG REST access is restricted to academic users; commercial use requires a separate license.
Results depend on live network access to rest.kegg.jp and current KEGG availability.
Helper functions return raw response text and provide limited network error handling.
Binary image responses may fail because the helper decodes every response as UTF-8.

use_cases.title: Map genes to pathways
use_cases.description: Find KEGG gene identifiers and retrieve their linked biological pathways.

use_cases.title: Integrate database identifiers
use_cases.description: Convert KEGG identifiers for integration with NCBI, UniProt, PubChem, or ChEBI datasets.

use_cases.title: Review drug interactions
use_cases.description: Retrieve KEGG interaction records for selected drug identifiers during nonclinical research.

prompt_templates.title: Find a gene
prompt_templates.prompt: Search KEGG genes for {gene_name} in {organism}. Return matching KEGG identifiers, names, and brief descriptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a gene name and organism.

prompt_templates.title: Map gene pathways
prompt_templates.prompt: For KEGG gene {gene_id}, list linked pathways. Summarize each pathway and retrieve details for the top {count} results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Connect one known gene to pathway context.

prompt_templates.title: Convert identifiers
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these KEGG identifiers to {target_database}: {identifiers}. Present matched and unmatched identifiers in separate tables.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare KEGG records for cross-database integration.

prompt_templates.title: Compare organism pathways
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare pathway {pathway_id} across {organisms}. Retrieve organism entries, linked genes, shared identifiers, and notable differences. State retrieval limits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Perform an advanced cross-organism pathway comparison.

output_examples.input: Find human KEGG genes matching p53.
output_examples.output: Matched hsa:7157, TP53. The result includes the KEGG identifier, gene symbol, and description.

output_examples.input: List pathways linked to human gene hsa:10458.
output_examples.output: A table lists each linked pathway identifier and name, followed by concise pathway context from KEGG.
The response pairs the KEGG gene identifier with its available UniProt identifier and notes unmatched results.

best_practices: Confirm organism codes and identifier formats before making requests.
Batch no more than ten entries and avoid rapid request sequences.
Preserve raw KEGG responses with retrieval dates before transforming results.
anti_patterns: Do not use the academic API for commercial work without KEGG licensing.
Do not treat KEGG drug interaction data as clinical advice.
Do not request pathway images with the current text-decoding helper.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: No. The helpers use public KEGG REST endpoints, subject to KEGG access and licensing terms.

faq.question: Can I use it for commercial work?
faq.answer: Not through the academic API terms. Contact KEGG for the required commercial license.

faq.question: Which KEGG operations are supported?
faq.answer: The helper supports information, list, find, get, conversion, link, and drug interaction operations.

faq.question: Can the helper download pathway images?
faq.answer: The endpoint option exists, but the current helper decodes responses as text. Use a binary-aware client for images.

faq.question: How should I limit requests?
faq.answer: Batch no more than ten entries and avoid rapid requests. KEGG documents special single-entry limits for several formats.

faq.question: Are results current and reproducible?
faq.answer: Live responses reflect the current KEGG service. Record retrieval dates and preserve raw responses for reproducibility.
